co_golden.blurb: Golden sits where the Front Range foothills meet the Denver metro area, and its climbing spreads across the canyon and mesa country around town. Clear Creek Canyon is the big one, a sport-heavy canyon on gneiss, schist and sandy granite with the odd trad line. North Table Mountain's cliff band is a busy local crag of short, closely bolted routes, with a lot of moderates. Golden Gate Canyon and Lookout Mountain Road add smaller venues. Sport routes lead the count, followed by trad and a sizeable bouldering scene. Most roped climbs fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with the thickest cluster around 5.10 to 5.11, and boulder problems span the whole V scale. Climbing continues year-round, and south and west facing walls stay comfortable in cold months.

co_fort_collins.blurb: Fort Collins climbing lies in the foothills just west of town and up the Cache la Poudre River canyon to the northwest. Bouldering makes up more than half of everything here, and the sandstone around Horsetooth Reservoir has been a bouldering haunt since the late 1960s, with Lory State Park adding granite boulders on the reservoir's northwest side. Poudre Canyon is the main roped destination, with Carter Lake and Red Feather Lakes rounding things out. Sport routes outnumber trad, and roped routes cluster at 5.10 to 5.12, while boulder problems run from very easy to hard, with plenty in the V0 to V6 range. Red Feather Lakes is newer and still being explored.

wv_northern_wv.blurb: Northern West Virginia is a bouldering region first, centred on Coopers Rock State Forest, which sits on the rim of the Cheat River gorge a short drive east of Morgantown off the interstate. The rock is coarse, gritty Pennsylvanian sandstone, split along joints into boulder fields, crevices and maze-like formations, with low cliffs that also suit top-roping. Nearly everything here is a boulder problem, from beginner scrambles to hard testpieces, with most problems between V0 and V5. Cheat Canyon, Valley Falls and North Bend State Park hold smaller collections of roped lines. Spring and fall bring the friendliest temperatures, summer shade helps under the forest canopy, and the rock needs time to dry after rain.

ca_los_angeles_basin.blurb: Climbing around greater Los Angeles is scattered across the mountains and coast ringing the basin. The San Gabriel Mountains of Angeles National Forest rise just north of the city, from chaparral foothills to pine and fir slopes above 10,000 feet. The Santa Monica Mountains, part of a large urban national park, hold popular crags in Malibu Creek State Park and Circle X Ranch. Bouldering and sport routes lead the count, with trad and top-rope lines behind them. Roped grades run from easy up through 5.13, most between 5.9 and 5.12, while problems run from V0 to the hard end. The Santa Ana Mountains and the beaches add further variety.

wa_leavenworth.blurb: Leavenworth is a Bavarian-styled town on the east side of the Cascades, and roughly fifty crags lie within ten miles of it. The cliffs are clean, solid granitic rock. Much of the climbing sits up Icicle Creek, where there are tall multi-pitch walls, single-pitch crags beside the road and a dense scatter of boulders. Boulder problems are the largest group, followed by trad and then sport, with a few ice routes in winter. Roped climbs mostly run 5.7 to 5.11 and peak around 5.10. Summers are dry thanks to the rain shadow, with guided climbing running April through October; winters are cold and snowy.
